page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance provisions 2 vCPUs backed by a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). The underlying processor includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography acceleration. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread performance alongside constrained overall throughput. The server scores 2292.0 in the Geekbench single-core test, placing it in the top tier, supported by strong gzip compression (34.76 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.76 GB/sec) rates. In contrast, multi-core capacity is bounded by the two-thread limit, registering a multi-core Geekbench score of 2816.0 and a multi-core stress-ng result of 2216.77. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 20.28 GB/sec for reads and 14.17 GB/sec for writes, which trails larger multi-channel configurations.

Cost efficiency is focused on entry-level, compute-centric workloads that require modern instruction sets without paying for excess RAM capacity or unneeded hardware accelerators. With no bundled local disks or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, storage and external connectivity rely on attached network infrastructure. The primary performance tradeoff centers on strong instruction execution per core versus minimal aggregate memory and parallel execution limits.

The c4-highcpu-2 instance is suitable for lightweight batch tasks, continuous integration and build nodes, microservices, entry-level text processing, and single-threaded utilities that benefit from AVX-512 and AMX vector capabilities.
